channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Democratic Senator Coons Says Secretary Lutnick Let America Down
item.description: Senator Chris Coons, a Democrat from Delaware, says Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick "let America down" and is at center of a controversy involving Nvidia. Senator Coons wants to know if Lutnick made it easier for China to secure Nvidia advanced AI chips. Coons says he has no "concrete evidence" that US national security has been compromised. President Donald Trump says he has complete confidence in Lutnick. Senator Coons speaks on "Bloomberg Surveillance." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Fed's Collins Talks Inflation Risks, Rate Policy and AI
item.description: Federal Reserve Bank of Boston President Susan Collins, discusses inflation risks, monetary policy and broader economic conditions during an interview with Michael McKee on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Collins says inflation remains too high and is showing signs of broadening beyond energy, with resilient demand and healthy growth supporting the case for additional policy tightening “soon." Collins also comments on the challenges facing the housing market and the economic impact of AI. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Cerebras Soars on Sales; Cisco Down on Expectations Miss | Stock Movers
item.description:
On this episode of Stock Movers:
- Shares of Cerebras Systems (CBRS) soared ahead of the US market open after the chipmaker gave a sales guidance well above estimates, while unveiling new deals with Oracle and Microsoft. A key investor concern is a rollout delay in the firm’s contract with OpenAI. - Shares of Cisco Systems (CSCO) declined in the early session after the networking gear maker reported a 21% rise in product orders in fiscal 1Q, missing expectations and marking a slowdown from the previous period. - Shares of Applied Materials (AMAT) inched higher after the company reported fourth-quarter results that beat expectations and gave an outlook for adjusted first-quarter earnings that is stronger than expected. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic IPO: AI’s $1.4T Test
item.description: Anthropic’s potential IPO is drawing extraordinary investor demand, with a reported target valuation of $1.4 trillion. Bloomberg’s Bailey Lipschultz joins Bloomberg Open Interest to explain why investors see the AI company as a must-own and why soaring compute costs, cash burn, uncertain profitability and unusual insider share sales could make the offering volatile. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Fundamentals Intact Despite Nvidia Fallout: Weaver
item.description: Michelle Weaver, head of US thematic research at Morgan Stanley, says AI fundamentals remain strong despite recent market volatility. “On both of those fronts, yes, we’re still seeing positive signals,” Weaver says on “Bloomberg Surveillance,” citing compute demand and gains from AI adoption. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Musk Bets Push Antonio Gracias’s Valor to Eye-Popping Returns
item.description: Valor Equity Partners founder Antonio Gracias has cashed in on the decades of bets he’s placed on his close friend Elon Musk’s companies: since 2003, Valor has delivered a 78% net return rate across all of its funds.
item.dc:creator: Carmen Arroyo

item.title: Microsoft Says Making Progress Fixing One of Its Longest Outages
item.description: Microsoft Corp. said it was making progress in efforts to restore access to its flagship software and end an outage that has paralyzed government offices, traders and businesses globally.
item.dc:creator: Matt Day

item.title: Disney Pivots to Embrace AI From Film to Parks
item.description: While remaining protective of its valuable intellectual property, Disney is infusing AI into operations across the board.
item.dc:creator: Dawn C. Chmielewski and Thomas Buckley

item.title: Neocloud Nscale Reveals $5.5 Billion Debt and Closer Nvidia Ties Ahead of IPO
item.description: Data center developer Nscale needs more cash, has significantly increased its debt and is more reliant on Nvidia Corp. than previously disclosed, it said in a regulatory filing ahead of its planned initial public offering.
item.dc:creator: Mark Bergen and Olivia Solon

item.title: Elon Musk’s SpaceX Starship: Why the Rocket Is Critical to Its Future
item.description: For the full experience visit: SpaceX’s Future Hinges on Starship. Can It Deliver?
item.dc:creator: Loren Grush and Stephanie Davidson

item.title: Nvidia’s Biggest Risk Is Product Pace: Windsor
item.description: Radio Free Mobile founder Richard Windsor says the immediate damage to Nvidia is reputational, with its products, contracts and financial outlook still intact. He says the critical test for Jensen Huang’s successor will be maintaining the rapid product-development cycle that underpinned Nvidia’s dominance and warns that any slowdown could cost the company market share and margins. Windsor was speaking to Tom Mackenzie on the latest episode of Bloomberg Tech: Europe which explored the risks and rewards for Europe following Jensen Huang's departure as Nvidia CEO. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Dan Ives on Nvidia Without Jensen Huang, Microsoft Outage
item.description: Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co., says that Nvidia without Jensen Huang “evens the playing field” in artificial intelligence and discusses why he thinks the next CEO will be from outside the company. Ives also addresses what he calls Microsoft’s “disaster moment” with disruptions for Outlook, Teams and the Copilot AI tool. He speaks on “Bloomberg Surveillance.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Jensen Huang’s Supporters See Nvidia Exit as Lesson for Founders to Keep Control
item.description: Silicon Valley supporters say CEO shouldn’t have given up control to Nvidia board
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Torrence

item.title: Businessweek In December Is All About China
item.description: China’s car business is miles ahead of the rest of the world. Brad Stone took a special look at its EV supremacy in Businessweek’s special December issue on the Asian nation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Dan Ives Cuts Nvidia Price Target, But Stays Bullish Post-Huang
item.description: Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co., says that Nvidia without Jensen Huang “evens the playing field” in artificial intelligence. Ives discusses Nvidia’s valuation without Huang, why he thinks the next CEO will be from outside the company and what challenges they may face. He speaks on “Bloomberg Surveillance.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia in Crisis: What Next? | Bloomberg Tech: Europe
item.description:
Nvidia faces is in crisis after the sudden departure of Jensen Huang, the rock star CEO who turned it into the company at the heart of the AI boom. As markets digest the fallout, the shockwaves are spreading across Europe’s technology ecosystem. In this special edition of Bloomberg Tech Europe, Tom Mackenzie explores what it means for the tech industry, investors and AI sovereignty in Europe.
"Bloomberg Tech: Europe" spotlights the biggest names and trends shaping the region's technology ecosystem as the global competition heats up. This monthly, 30-minute magazine-style show features in-depth interviews with top technology leaders, as well as major investors and policymakers - giving you a compelling A to Z of the most consequential innovations, opportunities and challenges.
Today's guests includes Richard Windsor, Radio Free Mobile Founder and Owner, Roxanne Varza, Station F Director, Dan Akarca, Callosum Co-Founder. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Microsoft Outage Sends Traders Back to Phones and Fax
item.description: Traders were forced to do business by phone and Whatsapp, and even fire up their fax machines, as a worldwide outage of Microsoft Corp. software crippled communications and snarled email services.
item.dc:creator: Ruth Carson, Bernadette Toh and Macarena Muñoz

item.title: Banned Nvidia Chips Installed at China Data Center Linked to Alice Huang
item.description: A Chinese company founded by Alice Huang, the woman at the center of a controversy dogging Nvidia Corp., procured smuggled AI chips that were installed at a Shanghai data center with links to Megaspeed International Pte, according to documents reviewed by Bloomberg News.
item.dc:creator: Andy Lin, Mackenzie Hawkins and Kari Lindberg

item.title: Samsung Is in Talks to Acquire Data Center Cooling Firm Modine
item.description: Samsung Electronics Co. is in talks to acquire Modine Manufacturing Co., a maker of cooling systems for data centers, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: David Carnevali and Ryan Gould

item.title: Cerebras Shares Jump Following Strong Quarterly Sales Outlook
item.description: Cerebras Systems Inc. shares jumped by the most in five months after the company gave a sales forecast for the current quarter that exceeded analysts’ estimates, signaling that a push to challenge Nvidia Corp. in artificial intelligence chips is paying off.
item.dc:creator: Ian King
